If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 3–5 days, accelerate upward correction in mid-horizon (8–15 days) by 1–2% to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment remains flat (0.00–0.33) across 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias in late horizon (16–30 days) to account for mean reversion.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00+ in last 2 days, apply a 1.0–2.0% upward adjustment in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect strong bullish sentiment.

If sentiment is mixed (±0.33) across 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% neutral adjustment in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overreacting to sentiment noise.
